page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-80 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 80 dedicated virtual CPUs across 40 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 320 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Each core provides 32 KB of L1 data cache and 0.5 MB of L2 cache, complemented by 32 MB of L3 cache. There are no hardware GPUs included, and no local ephemeral storage is bundled, requiring workloads to rely on attached persistent storage volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and memory throughput characteristics. The instance achieved a multi-core score of 107964.98 on stress-ng and a PassMark CPU score of 69828.6, placing both metrics in the top 25 percent. Cryptographic performance is particularly notable, scoring 85389.14 in PassMark CPU encryption tests (top 10 percent) due to hardware-assisted AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 200.15 GB/s, with write speeds of 123.81 GB/s. In-memory data access is reflected in Redis throughput reaching 77.46 million SET operations per second and static web serving throughput measuring 47.97 GB/s. Moderate results are observed in Geekbench single-core (1506.0) and multi-core (14839.0) testing, alongside CPU-based LLM inference, which is limited by the absence of AVX-512 instruction extensions.

The dense allocation of 80 vCPUs and 320 GB of memory makes the n2d-standard-80 cost-effective for enterprise workloads that require heavy multi-threading and substantial memory overhead without specialized accelerator premiums. Typical deployment targets include distributed caching layers, large-scale Redis instances, enterprise web application servers, relational database management systems, and parallel data transformation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-80 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 80 vCPUs (40 physical cores) powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 320 GB of RAM. The instance features a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio, dedicated core allocations, and robust cryptographic hardware support including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. It includes no local storage or GPUs, operating exclusively with network-attached storage. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-threaded capabilities, registering 107964.98 in stress-ng multi-core testing, top-tier encryption metrics, and high-throughput memory operations with Redis achieving 77.46 million SET operations per second. While single-thread execution and instruction-heavy tasks are constrained by the lack of AVX-512 extensions, its multi-core density delivers strong resource efficiency. It is well matched for large-scale web serving, distributed caching, databases, and continuous integration clusters.
